note: spec_peak for the strict bound (roadmap 4.5): the most the implementation can serve, never a measurement. Where a figure is uncertain the GENEROUS end is taken, because a generous peak can only lower the bound (a looser, still valid eta); a stingy one could let a measurement beat its bound. Unit: per second.

sm_clock_max_hz.source: nvidia-smi -q -d CLOCK, Max Clocks SM = 3003 MHz (driver 580.95.05); the default application clock is 2418 MHz

vendor_fp32.source: NVIDIA, via The Register 2025-08-27 (Hot Chips): 'about 31 teraFLOPS of single precision'

vendor_fp4_sparse.source: NVIDIA: '1 petaFLOP of FP4 with sparsity'

system_cache_bytes.source: The Register 2025-08-27 (Hot Chips): GB10 has a 16 MB system-level ('L4') cache shared by the CPU and GPU. Counted as write-back capacity: if it does not hold GPU writes, the bound is only looser

fp32_fma.derivation: 48 SM x 128 FP32 FMA/clk/SM (CUDA C Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput, compute capability 12.x) x 3.003e9 Hz = 18.45e12 FMA/s = 36.9 TFLOPS, above the vendor 31 TFLOPS (which is at a lower clock): generous

fp16_fma_simt.derivation: half2 doubles the FP32 rate: 2 x 18.45e12

tensor_fp16_mac.derivation: upper estimate from the vendor figure: 1e15 FP4 sparse FLOPS = 5e14 dense; Blackwell halves the rate at each doubling of operand width (FP4 -> FP8 -> FP16), giving 1.25e14 FP16 dense FLOPS at the clock the vendor quotes (taken as the 2418 MHz default); scaled to the 3003 MHz maximum = 1.5525e14 FLOPS = 7.7625e13 MAC/s. If the per-SM figure is lower (512 FLOP/clk/SM gives 3.69e13 MAC/s), this only loosens the bound.

sfu.derivation: 48 SM x 16 MUFU/clk/SM x 3.003e9 (CUDA C Programming Guide, cc 12.x); scoped only -- a transcendental can also be built from FMAs

dram_bytes.derivation: 256 bit / 8 x 8533e6 transfers/s = 273.1 GB/s. Valid as a bound only under the cold-L2 protocol (archbench/PROTOCOL.md): data starts in DRAM because L2 is flushed before every timed call

caches.note: L2 + system cache. Outputs that fit may stay dirty in cache when the kernel ends, so only writes BEYOND this capacity are a necessary DRAM transfer; the flush before a timed call is twice this size so required READS do come from DRAM
